_comment: REQUEST-PARITY BASELINE. Two sections, one per direction, both read by tests/contract-parity.test.ts and both shrink-only: `unknown_keys` = a key the inputSchema declares and the route rules() do not; `missing_keys` = a key the route accepts and the inputSchema omits (the optional-field gate, added 2026-08-18; the required half fails outright and is never baselined). An entry that stopped drifting FAILS the gate and prints the line to delete. In `missing_keys` only, `"tool": "*"` waives one path across the service: it is for class-wide facts (today: the legacy `limit` alias of `page_size`), never for a tool-specific hole.
every inputSchema key the route rules() does not declare is either fixed on the tool or listed
here with the reason it is not. IT MAY ONLY SHRINK. An entry that stopped drifting FAILS the
gate and prints the line to delete, exactly like ratchet.json and the two allow-lists next to it,
so the list cannot quietly grow into a blanket skip. Adding a line is a deliberate, reviewable act:
it records debt, it does not excuse it.
The other three request gates (required-field, bound, enum) carry NO baseline, by design: their
drift was driven to zero on 2026-07-27 and every one of those classes is a tool-side fix.
118 -> 29 on 2026-07-27: the whole metrics class is gone, paid off rather than re-worded. It was
89 lines across the 8 *_metrics tools, one silent-wrong-answer bug wearing two faces, and each
face got the fix its own side needed:
- gtm.service.linkedin (69): metrics() there builds no {Entity}Filter at all. It reads one or two
hand-picked keys off input(filter) and drops the rest, so the TOOLS were narrowed to exactly
what the aggregation applies (linkedin_account_sid everywhere, plus status on the activity log).
- gtm.service.id (20): the opposite. The controller builds the {Entity}Filter and hands it whole
to counts() and metrics(), so every axis WAS applied and none of the missing ones was validated.
The three MetricsRequests now declare the full filter. The time axes are the subtle part:
billing/credit null theirs so the period stays the one window for the sums, but counts() carries
no period of its own and does apply them, so they are declared too. (2026-08-16: the credit one
went with the platform-wide credits removal. gtm.service.id ships three MetricsRequests today,
a different three: api-keys, billing-transactions, notifications.)
- the 90th line, get_notifications_metrics.group_by, was the same defect on a different key: the
tool and the research both had it, the backend read it nowhere. NotificationService::metricsGroups()
now exists and the rule is Rule::in the groupable enum.
None of this widened a waiver. What is left is the four classes below.
What is in here today, by class:
1. 14 account-share filter operators. The SearchRequest enumerates .eq / .in per field; FilterOp
accepts the whole operator set and McpFormRequest reads input(filter), so .ne / .nin / .is_null
are applied but unvalidated.
2. 7 include params the SearchRequest never declares. Four work anyway (the controller reads
input(include)); three name documented relations no controller builds. Nine more of this class
were fixed instead, with .omit({ include: true }), where the tool named no relation at all.
3. (retired 2026-08-14) The 4 linkedin_tracked_post_sid inputs are gone: A12 dropped the arm
from the three post tools, so the schemas and the FormRequests agree on a required post.
4. 3 singles: one api-keys filter axis, one connection-requests filter axis, and the add-addon
idempotency token. That last one is the only entry here that is a PROMISE rather than a
missing validation, and it sits on a verb that charges a card: pay it off by implementing the
replay or by dropping the field, not by leaving it.
(paid off 2026-08-20) The antidetect BYO-proxy credential pair is gone: the connect modal now
collects username/password, so AntidetectBrowserCreateRequest declares them like update-proxy
already did, and they no longer travel unvalidated.

linkedin.reason: legacy `limit` alias of `page_size`, kept on the search FormRequests for the table frontends that still send it. Tools speak the cursor contract (`page_size` + `cursor`) and must not learn a second spelling of the same knob: two page-size keys on one tool is a 422 waiting for whichever the agent picks second. Class-wide by design (`tool: "*"`): one decision, not forty lines. Delete when the alias leaves the FormRequests.

GET /api/antidetect-browsers/{sid} is bound to AntidetectBrowserSearchRequest, the SEARCH FormRequest, so its rule set describes a list call: this tool reads ONE row by sid and the controller passes none of these through. Delete when the show action gets a FormRequest of its own.

run and stop share AntidetectBrowserActionRequest, and `now` is stop's shortcut (commit `stopped` at once instead of waiting for the node teardown). On run it is accepted and ignored, so offering it would advertise a knob that does nothing. stop_antidetect_browser declares it.

metrics tools were deliberately narrowed to the axes the aggregation applies (2026-07-27, the same call recorded under unknown_keys): this one aggregates over the window alone, so a filter the tool advertised would be silently dropped.
